raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a large, dense opacity occupying the right hemithorax with a meniscus sign and blunting of the costophrenic angle, which are classic features of a pleural effusion. The significant mass effect from this fluid collection pushes the mediastinum and trachea to the contralateral (left) side, distinguishing it from atelectasis (which would cause ipsilateral deviation) or pneumonia (which typically lacks such severe shift).
